development_note: the integrator approved the associated-unsafe notice (obj/parallel/associated-unsafe/notice.md, sha256 83df7582) and movers M1, M2 with M2a, M3 and M4 by name before this file. The base-pin exploration (obj/parallel/associated-unsafe/explore) ran the fixture's safe twins and the generated providers before this declaration; it is evidence for nothing, and fixed only the older-profile and trait-default first fences recorded as such. The self-demand probe ran before this declaration and passed its assertions (`unsafe_methods_install_at_their_safe_twins_cost` under fastcheck, obj/parallel/associated-unsafe/runs/probe2.log); a first run stopped at a borrow error in the forgery helper, fixed before the rerun. Departures from the notice, declared here: the scaling and probe twins are called in the same unsafe block, so that only flag bytes differ, as the notice's equal-length prediction requires (in a twin the block holds no unsafe operation, so rustc would warn `unused_unsafe`; the twins run only in RustGM's in-process tests, whose frontend has no such lint, and are not oracle inputs); the older-profile controls and forgeries use the nominals provider, which all three versions export; the base-pin exploration showed versions 10 and 12 stopping a unit struct at `source declaration kind is outside the initial source profile`, so the older trait controls implement for u8 and the older inherent control uses a record struct, which stops at its conformance record as const-methods recorded; forged row 8 forges the u8 impl's trait member `via`, since older profiles stop every inherent impl there
